Extremely Disappointing Experience – Would Not Recommend

We recently hosted a wedding function at this hall, and it was one of the most stressful experiences we’ve ever had. From the beginning, the management was unprofessional, disorganized, and completely unresponsive to our concerns.

The biggest issue was the attendant, Ruchika. Her behavior throughout the event was rude, dismissive, and unhelpful. She lacked basic courtesy and professionalism. Whenever we raised concerns about arrangements, cleanliness, or coordination, she either ignored us or responded with an attitude. On such an important day, the last thing anyone needs is additional stress caused by staff behavior.

The hall itself was poorly maintained. Despite prior assurances, cleanliness was below expectations — restrooms were not properly cleaned, decorations were not arranged as discussed, and basic coordination between staff members was missing. Several promised arrangements were either delayed or not delivered at all.

The air conditioning was inconsistent, guests had to repeatedly ask for basic assistance, and overall event management was chaotic. There was no sense of accountability from the management team. Even simple requests were treated as inconveniences.

For the amount charged, the quality of service was unacceptable. A wedding is a once-in-a-lifetime event, and this venue failed to deliver even basic standards of hospitality and professionalism.

I would strongly advise future couples to think carefully before booking this hall. Based on our experience, it caused unnecessary stress on what should have been a joyful occasion.

featured_reviews.name: Rehan Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst Wedding Venue Experience – Absolute Mismanagement and Broken Promises

If I could give Sawai Banquet Hall zero stars, I would.

What was supposed to be one of the most important and memorable days of our lives turned into a stressful and frustrating experience because of the venue's complete lack of professionalism, planning, and accountability. The management made countless promises before taking our booking, but when it came time to deliver, they failed on almost every front.

We were explicitly assured that the afternoon event would end by 4:30 PM and that all the venues we had booked Sawai Banquet, Tiara, Ahana, and Vatika  would be fully handed over by 5:30 PM. However, when we arrived at 6:15 PM, the previous event's guests were still vacating the premises. The venue was nowhere close to being ready. Decorations had not been completed, arrangements were unfinished, and there was complete chaos instead of preparation.

The bridal room was another disappointment. The air conditioning was not working, making it extremely uncomfortable for the bride and family members during an already hectic schedule.

The washrooms were dirty, unhygienic, and clearly had not been cleaned properly despite repeated assurances regarding venue cleanliness. For a premium wedding venue, this level of neglect is simply unacceptable.

Several arrangements that were specifically promised during discussions were never provided. Direction boards for the Veg and Non-Veg food sections were missing. The Nikah setup was not arranged as committed. Guests were left confused and inconvenienced due to the lack of basic event coordination.

The situation only worsened during the reception. Even by 8:00 PM, the special reception entry that had been promised was still not ready. Chairs and sofas were covered in dust and looked as though they had not been cleaned before guests arrived. It was embarrassing to host guests under such conditions.

Parking arrangements were another complete failure. We were charged for parking facilities for approximately 30 vehicles and were informed that the venue had a tie-up with Amar Theatre to accommodate additional parking. On the wedding day, we were suddenly informed that the theatre was undergoing demolition and no parking was available. No alternative arrangements were made, leaving our guests to struggle unnecessarily.

What is most disappointing is not just the poor execution, but the complete gap between what was promised and what was delivered. The management seems far more interested in making commitments during the sales process than actually fulfilling them on the event day.

This venue excels at making promises and fails at keeping them.

Our wedding day should have been filled with joy and celebration. Instead, we spent hours dealing with delays, missing arrangements, poor cleanliness, and management failures.

I would strongly advise anyone planning a wedding or major event to avoid Sawai Banquet Hall unless they are prepared for last-minute surprises, broken commitments, and unnecessary stress.

Tall promises. Zero delivery. Zero accountability. Absolutely not recommended.

My overall experience at this place was quite disappointing, and I honestly feel it is overrated. While the décor and overall ambience are visually appealing and thoughtfully designed, the service quality does not match the expectations created by the appearance. The interiors are well done and give a good first impression, but unfortunately, that is where the positives end.

One major issue I faced was the lack of basic facilities. Drinking water was not provided during the night, which is a fundamental necessity for any guest. It was inconvenient and uncomfortable to not have access to something so essential. Additionally, there was no proper system or designated place for garbage disposal. Guests were expected to manage and dispose of waste on their own, which is not ideal and feels unprofessional.

Good décor alone cannot compensate for poor service and inadequate facilities. Hospitality should prioritize guest comfort and convenience, and in this case, those aspects were clearly lacking. With better service management and attention to basic amenities, the experience could improve significantly. Until then, I would not consider it worth the hype.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Atarah Banquet: A name you can trust for all your celebrations.
We recently hosted our son’s first birthday here, and we cannot stop praising this venue. Below is our honest and detailed review:

From my very first enquiry call, I was introduced to Ms. Mamta Jain, the main coordinator for our event. Mamta is someone you can share ideas with, and she will make them happen. Kudos to her for being patient and supportive through every call, message, and in-person meeting.

We opted for the Gold package (veg and non-veg), which included:

• 2 welcome drinks
• 2–3 starters
• 3 main course dishes
• 2 types of rice
• 1 dal dish
• 3 varieties of Indian breads
• 3 desserts
• 1 ice cream

We also added a Pan counter at a nominal cost. The best part of Atarah’s packages is the flexibility—you can customize everything to your preferences. For example, although the package included a Chinese dish, we replaced it with a Chaat counter (3 dishes), which turned out to be a fantastic choice.

Our menu selections:

• Welcome drinks: Watermelon cooler (mojito) and Guava chilli
• Starters (10/10):• Veg: Cheese corn balls, Veg spring rolls (not on the menu, but Atarah graciously obliged)
• Non-veg: Chicken chilli, Chicken tikka

• Main course (10/10):• Rice: Jeera rice, Dum biryani (veg & non-veg)
• Dal fry
• Veg: Tawa bhaji, Paneer lababdar, Dum aloo
• Non-veg: Chicken kadai, Chicken Afghani, Mutton sukha

• Indian breads (10/10): Puri, Butter roti, Garlic naan
• Desserts (10/10): Aamras, Angoor basundi, Rabdi jalebi• Special mention: The Aamras was the highlight—every guest went back for seconds!

• Ice cream (9/10): Kulfi slice
• Chaat (10/10): Pani puri, Katori chaat, Ragda patties
• Pan counter (10/10)

The package also included papad, pickle, mukhwas, and mineral water (200 ml).

We added activities like caricature and face painting. While the services were enjoyable, one regret was that the caricature artists left after two hours despite being booked for 200 guests. Unfortunately, even we—the hosts—didn’t get our portraits done.

Aside from this minor hiccup, everything else was flawless. From decorations (lights, stage, hall, seating) to music, food, and service, Atarah delivered perfection. Both Ms. Mamta and Mr. Jayesh coordinated with us until the very end, ensuring the event ran smoothly.

Final verdict:
Atarah Banquets exceeded our expectations and made our son’s first birthday truly memorable. We wholeheartedly recommend them to friends and family.

featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are looking for a venue that balances budget and elegance in the eastern suburbs, City Banquet is a solid contender! 🏙️

**The Vibe & Decor** ✨
The hall has a very modern and clean aesthetic. The lighting is bright and festive, making it perfect for weddings, sangeets, or big birthday bashes. They have a spacious layout that doesn’t feel cramped even with a decent crowd. 💡🎊

**The Food** 🍲
The catering is one of the highlights! 🥘 Whether you're going for the Veg or Non-Veg spread, the flavors are authentic and the variety is impressive. The starters are usually a hit with the guests! 😋🍗

**Location & Accessibility** 📍
Located right on the **Ghatkopar-Mankhurd Link Road**, it is super easy for guests to find. It’s well-connected to both the Eastern Express Highway and the Navi Mumbai side. 🚗🛣️

**Pros:**

* **Ample Parking:** Unlike many Mumbai venues, they actually have decent space for vehicles. 🅿️✅.

* **Friendly Staff:** The management is cooperative and helps with the minute-to-minute flow of the event. 🤝

* **Great AC:** Keeping the Mumbai heat out is a priority, and their cooling system does the job well! ❄️💨

**Cons:**

* **Basement Access:** Note that the hall is in the basement, and the lack of an elevator can be a bit tricky for elderly guests. 🪜⚠️

* **Peak Hour Traffic:** Since it's on a main link road, traffic during evening muhrats can be a bit of a nightmare. 🚦😫

**Final Verdict:** A fantastic "value-for-money" venue for mid-sized gatherings (up to 400-450 people). It looks premium without the premium price tag! 💰💎

**Would I recommend it?** Yes! Just make sure to assist any elderly guests with the stairs. 👍🙌
